details: Yemeni Houthi forces have claimed responsibility for fresh attacks on Saudi Arabian oil infrastructure, including the Ras Tanura refinery (Saudi Arabia's largest) and the Jazan refinery. These incidents, alongside reported attacks on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, have intensified concerns about crude supply disruptions in the Middle East. Oil prices (Brent and WTI) have consequently rallied, with Brent crude futures trading above $97 per barrel, marking its first weekly gain this month. The ongoing uncertainty surrounding the OPEC+ meeting, where output targets for Q1 2027 are being discussed, further contributes to market volatility.
title: Houthi Attacks on Saudi Oil Facilities Spur Oil Price Rally

details: European stock markets experienced significant declines due to escalating concerns over potential energy shortages. This follows Russian energy giant Gazprom's announcement that its key Nord Stream pipeline, a major gas supplier to Europe, would remain shut indefinitely due to an oil leak. Compounding the issue, a cold snap is threatening to accelerate withdrawals from already depleted European gas reserves, pushing benchmark natural gas prices higher.
sourceName: Al Jazeera / Investing.com (citing energy market data)
title: European Stocks Fall Amid Energy Shortage Fears, Gas Prices Climb

details: The Office of the US Trade Representative has proposed a fresh round of tariffs on imports from 14 economies, including a 20% tariff on China and 15% on the European Union. These proposed tariffs, reportedly using Section 301 to re-establish a previous tariff regime, are contributing to renewed trade policy uncertainty and have been noted as a factor in global market volatility. China has previously issued "blocking orders" in response to US sanctions.
sourceName: UBS Global (referencing US Trade Representative proposal)
title: New US Tariffs on China and EU Raise Trade War Concerns

details: Global stock markets have experienced recent volatility, particularly in the technology sector, driven by concerns over the financial viability and sustainability of AI infrastructure investments. This broader macroeconomic pressure, coupled with persistent inflation and a stronger US dollar, is weighing on overall market liquidity. Analysts suggest that Bitcoin's recovery may face prolonged consolidation rather than a swift rebound, despite signs of selling pressure exhaustion and historically low valuations, as investors remain cautious amidst these uncertainties.
title: AI Investment Doubts & Macro Headwinds Stall Bitcoin Recovery
